### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, touching **54** documentable anchor(s).

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx`  _(via email_template (literal, a string literal in runApply; a string literal in runTemplatePromotion; a string literal in save), sys_email_template (literal, a string literal in TEMPLATE_OBJECT))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via email_template (literal, a string literal in runApply; a string literal in runTemplatePromotion; a string literal in save))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via sys_setting (literal, a string literal in SETTINGS))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via sys_setting (literal, a string literal in SETTINGS))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via email_template (literal, a string literal in runApply; a string literal in runTemplatePromotion; a string literal in save), sys_setting (literal, a string literal in SETTINGS))_
- `content/docs/deployment/install-modes.mdx`  _(via email_template (literal, a string literal in runApply; a string literal in runTemplatePromotion; a string literal in save))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via managed_by (literal, a string literal in templatePromotionSql))_
- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`  _(via os migrate organization-ownership (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`  _(via os migrate organization-ownership (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via sys_email_template (literal, a string literal in TEMPLATE_OBJECT), sys_platform_setting (literal, a string literal in PLATFORM_SETTINGS), sys_setting (literal, a string literal in SETTINGS))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via sys_setting (literal, a string literal in SETTINGS))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via managed_by (literal, a string literal in templatePromotionSql))_
- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via managed_by (literal, a string literal in templatePromotionSql))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via sys_email_template (literal, a string literal in TEMPLATE_OBJECT))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via sys_setting (literal, a string literal in SETTINGS))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via body_text (symbol, a field of interface EmailTemplateRowForDefinition))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 35 pages)`
- **16** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **46** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 614fdec83280704418266aba83fb33dce1e5fb45` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dd7d87df9e2ed32326c1bf69920c8b0aa618c697` — the merge of head `db2088648cc2933d87102a010c2c89c25ea338fe` into base `614fdec83280704418266aba83fb33dce1e5fb45`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dd7d87df9e2ed32326c1bf69920c8b0aa618c697 && git checkout dd7d87df9e2ed32326c1bf69920c8b0aa618c697
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 614fdec83280704418266aba83fb33dce1e5fb45 db2088648cc2933d87102a010c2c89c25ea338fe && git checkout -B drift-repro 614fdec83280704418266aba83fb33dce1e5fb45 && git merge --no-ff db2088648cc2933d87102a010c2c89c25ea338fe

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 614fdec83280704418266aba83fb33dce1e5fb45
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 614fdec83280704418266aba83fb33dce1e5fb45` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `34989ec72ec0ed045fc09d80bc6fafbe0021c709`
Local-runs: none

**What was reviewed.** PR #23329 (`feat(cli,core): the organization-ownership ceremony promotes customized email templates and moves the settings global rung (C7b, PR 3 of 3)`, draft, base `main`, head repo = base repo) at head `34989ec72e`, the head the brief named; it had not moved at 2026-10-13T20:05Z. Seven commits over `origin/main` `4d4040ccb6`, which is also the merge-base: `0555b80a` and `5a05cb3d` (the PR 2 build and an early merge), `691bb957` (core mapper), `49d85fc6` (the two steps), `f36a3a34` (the merge that resolved against PR 2's squash `2808069121`), `636f149b` (changeset), `34989ec7` (merge of two `main` commits touching none of this PR's files). Three-dot diff: 8 files, +704 / −41, under `packages/cli`, `packages/core/src/security` and two changesets; the merge ref `06d8ebaf` (parents `4d4040cc`, `34989ec7`) has a tree byte-equal to the head's, so every check-run below ran on the diff as it would land. The apply module, its test and the command are unchanged on `main` since `2808069121`, so `git diff 2808069121 head` on those three files is PR 3's layer exactly. Inputs: card #22937's body, the claim 6122368393, the ruling 6138591940, the seat's answers 6140351542, the landing record 6151058104, the dispatch 6151180611, the dev's report 6153947869; PR 2's records 6147223040 and 6150575317; the PR body, file list, diff and merge ref; ADR-0131 on `origin/main` (1.4, D7, D10, D13, section 6 Q1); the head's check-runs. For the door and the schema: `EmailTemplateDefinitionSchema` (`packages/spec/src/system/email-template.zod.ts`), `itemDiscriminator` / `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` (`packages/metadata-core/src/item-key-discriminators.ts`), `saveMetaItem` and `readFlattenedMetaItems` in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, `sys-metadata-repository.ts`, the three object definitions, the inventory entries, `predicateSql` / `Sql` / `walkNullRows` in the plan module, `scripts/check-closing-target-claim.mjs` and `claimedBranches`.

**Check-runs on `34989ec7` at 2026-10-13T20:05Z:** 38 runs. 24 `success` (among them `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue`, `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path`). 6 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix row, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance). **7 still running: `Test Core (1/6)` through `(6/6)` and `Type Check · workspace`.** **1 `failure`: `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`** (job 115507157834, step 4 red; the log download is refused by the session's proxy, so the cause is read from the script and the card, not the log — see ③ F1).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The merge resolution — PR 2's landed behaviour holds, with one named semantic change, the dev's own.** Read off `git diff 2808069121 head -- organization-ownership-apply.ts`:
   - B1's provenance keep: `deletableWhere` still adds the `managed_by IS NULL OR NOT IN (package, platform, system)` keep on every table carrying `managed_by` — except, under `single`, on `sys_email_template` after the promotion (the discharge, below). The `CASE WHEN claim THEN 1 WHEN NOT (claim) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END = 0` keep is byte-identical, so a NULL-evaluating claim still keeps its row.
   - B2's departure count: `remainingFor` for `attribution` and `report` tables is unchanged (`rowsToAttribute + departingRows`); `TableOutcome.departures` is still filtered to rows above zero; `notNull` is overridden from the same list (now a local `departures` array, equal to the old one unless the walled template entry is pushed).
   - The gate re-read: `runMirrorDeletion` still calls `verifyReferences` before any DELETE and returns `blocked` without deleting. Keyset paging: `readAll` (id greater than the last page's id, bound, `LIMIT PAGE`) is unchanged and both new steps read through it. Checkpoint and marker: the loop, the per-step `ledger.write({ complete: false })`, the digest-bound checkpoint, the final `passed: complete && blocking === 0` are untouched; the two new steps are checkpointed like the others. `Sql.q` on every identifier and every value bound: holds on the old code and on the new (①7).
   - Changes to PR 2's lines that are not pure additions: `CEREMONY_STEPS` gains two members between `authored-conversion` and `rewrite`; `MetadataDoorPort.save` widens its type union; `ApplyOptions` gains a required `templates` port; `TableOutcome` gains `movedOut` / `movedIn`; `SEEDED_BY` moves up the file unchanged; and **the one behavioural change: under `single`, for `sys_email_template` only, `deletableWhere` skips the `template-promotion` and `organization-stamped` category keeps and the provenance keep** (`DISCHARGED_BY_PROMOTION`). The dev named it; its consequences are in ①2 and ③ F2. The test moved the "killed mid-step" trigger from `/^DELETE/` to `/^DELETE FROM "sys_capability"/` and excluded `sys_setting` / `sys_platform_setting` from the no-delete pin because the settings move now deletes before the rewrite; both test-only and honest.

2. **The promotion population — B1's kept set minus the seeded uncustomized organization-stamped copies, which is the dispatch's set; one deletion path escapes it.** `templatePromotionSql` selects `customized = true OR customized IS NULL OR managed_by IS NULL OR managed_by NOT IN (package, platform, system)` (values bound), with no organization clause. B1's kept set on this table is that same predicate OR `organization_id IS NOT NULL`. The difference — seeded, uncustomized, organization-stamped rows — is not promoted and, under `single`, is deleted as a mirror because the `organization-stamped` keep is discharged: the seat's answer 6140351542, applied as written. No row PR 2 deletes (seeded, uncustomized, NULL organization) is in the population. The `customized IS NULL` rows the dev added are right: B1's ELSE arm keeps them, so they are in the kept set; promoting an unknown is the safe direction, and when the body equals the served template the save is skipped (`alreadyPromoted`) before the row goes. On a table without `managed_by` the predicate is `1 = 1` (everything promoted, then under `single` everything deleted) — the safe direction, unmeasured. **Where a row can be deleted that should have been promoted:** under `single` the template DELETE is `WHERE 1 = 1` — the discharge removes every keep and the inventory names no mirror selector — and `promoted` is derived from the posture alone, not from a verified promotion of each row. In the same run every population row was promoted, `alreadyPromoted` or blocked (a blocker stops the ceremony before the DELETE), with two exceptions: a row with no name is "reported, never promoted" and the step still ends `done`, so the DELETE takes it; and on a **resumed run** (`template-promotion` checkpointed, `mirror-deletion` not) the promotion is skipped, `run.saved` is empty, nothing re-reads the table, and every row present is deleted — including one a 17.x admin customized or authored between the runs. PR 2 built the grant re-read for exactly this window and pinned it; the template step has no equivalent. ③ F2.

3. **What promotion writes.** Door: `protocol.saveMetaItem({ type: 'email_template', name, item: body, actor: 'os migrate organization-ownership' })`, the same door as the authored conversion. Mode defaults to `publish` (protocol.ts: "Default is 'publish'"), which the repository writes as `state: 'active'`; the request carries no organization and the door refuses organization-scoped writes for every type, so the row is environment-level (`organization_id` NULL); `bundle_member` comes from `itemDiscriminator('email_template', body)` — the body's `locale`, canonical `en-US` stored as NULL — so a second locale of one name is a second row under the `(type, name, organization_id, package_id, bundle_member)` key, and "one per (name, locale)" holds through the door. Owner: whatever the door stamps for the actor string; the mapper sends no provenance key. Posture: `single` only; under a wall nothing is written. **Idempotent:** the command's `find` reads `sys_metadata` (`type`, `name`, `state = 'active'`, `organization_id IS NULL`, `bundle_member = locale OR (NULL AND locale = 'en-US')`, all bound), then `getMetaItemsForExecution({ type: 'email_template' })` (returns `{ type, items }`, matched on `name` and `locale` with the `en-US` fallback); an equal body is `alreadyPromoted`, a differing environment row is a blocker ("never overwritten"), a differing served package item is overridden (D6: the environment row replaces the managed item whole), a door refusal is a blocker. **Equal to the served template:** no save, the row is then deleted — nothing lost. Caveat, unmeasured: `bodyKey` compares the body's own keys with `?? null`; if the real door normalizes a stored body so any of those keys differ, a re-run with rows still present (interrupted before deletion, checkpoint discarded by a digest change) reads a false "differs" blocker — loud, not lossy. **Deleted afterwards, and only after the write is verified:** deleted afterwards, yes; the verification is the door's acceptance in the same run and nothing on a resumed run (①2, F2).

4. **Counting until promotion.** Under `single`: a blocked promotion stops the ceremony, `complete: false`, `blocking` = blocker count, the ledger write has `passed: false` so `verified_at` stays null, and the blocker names the template `(name, locale)` and the row ids — pinned. After a completed promotion the discharge makes every remaining row deletable, mirror deletion removes them, and `remainingFor` reads 0 — pinned (the acceptance case ends `sys_email_template` empty, `complete: true, blocking: 0`). Under a wall: `remainingFor` adds the unpromoted count, the post-check pushes a synthetic `template-promotion` departure (`as: 'moved'`, label naming the posture, rows), `notNull.willReceive` reads false with that label, `blocking` is non-zero, `verified_at` null — pinned (`isolated`, `tpl_admin` counted, `tpl_seeded` deleted). The dev's two ablations (count dropped: the walled case red; population dropped: three cases red) are reported with restored blobs; weighed, not repeated. **Honest in the JSON:** yes — `tables[].departures[]` carries `id`, `label`, `as`, `rows`; `movedOut` / `movedIn` reconcile `before − deleted − movedOut + movedIn = after`, pinned per table. **In the human face:** the departure line prints through the existing loop; but the table filter still reads `attributed + deleted + unattributable + remaining + departures.length`, so `sys_setting` (movedOut 2) and `sys_platform_setting` (movedIn 2) print no table line — the move is visible only in the step line's summary `{"moved":2,"alreadyMoved":0}` and the progress line. Face nit, not blocking. Nit: `as: 'moved'` on a promotion stretches the inventory's two-word vocabulary.

5. **The global-rung move.** Destination `sys_platform_setting` (D7; inventory label "moved to sys_platform_setting (value_enc copied verbatim, one row per key)"). Population: the inventory departure's `where` (`scope = 'global'`), read through `predicateSql`, keyed `(namespace, key)`, compared on `value`, `value_enc`, `encrypted`, `locked`, `locked_reason`. Conflict rule: differing source rows for one key — blocker, nothing touched; target holds the key with a different value — blocker, nothing moved or deleted for that key (pinned, `mail.transport` with `"ses"`); target holds it equal — the source row is deleted only (`alreadyMoved`); target absent — `INSERT INTO to (shared cols) SELECT shared cols FROM from WHERE id = ?` (the columns are the intersection of the two physical column lists, each through `Sql.q`; the id bound), then `DELETE FROM from WHERE (scope = ?) AND id IN (?…)`. Target table absent — blocker with the remedy (boot once, re-run). **Verified before delete:** by the driver accepting the INSERT; no read-back of the target by key before the DELETE (the mirror step counts after its DELETE; this step does not). **Idempotent and interruption-safe:** the step is checkpointed only when done; interrupted between INSERT and DELETE, the next run finds the target equal and only deletes; a run after completion reads zero rows. **After the step** the plan's recount of the departure reads 0 (pinned: `sys_setting` departures `[]`), and `declared-rule-mirrors` still counts and is named (pinned, `rule_declared`). Two notes, not blocking: (a) the move takes every `scope = 'global'` row whatever its `organization_id`, while the departure it executes is counted by `walkNullRows` over NULL rows only; the settings service wrote global rows with `organization_id: null` (settings-service.ts line 2087), so the sets coincide today, but a stamped global row, if one existed, would be copied into a deployment-wide table — one organization's value becoming everyone's, the exact thing ①2 refuses under a wall. One bound clause (`organization_id IS NULL`) and a reported residue closes it. (b) The id is copied verbatim; a PK collision in the target throws through `execute` and aborts the run resumably, with the driver's message. The move runs before the rewrite gate: it is a departure, not fate 2, so D10's "mirror deletion behind the verified rewrite" does not reach it; the running 17.x service already serves the rung from the new table, so a later blocker leaves nothing broken.

6. **Core's `emailTemplateDefinitionFromRow`.** Against the strict schema (`strictObject`): the body carries `name`, `label`, `locale`, `subject`, `bodyHtml`, `variables`, `active` always and `bodyText`, `fromOverride`, `replyTo`, `description` when filled — every one a declared key; `protection` (no column), the retired `category` / `isSystem` and every state or provenance column are left out. `fromOverride` is `{ name?, address }`, the shape of `EmailAddressInlineSchema`; `label` falls back to the name (required string); `locale` falls back to `'en-US'`, equal to `EMAIL_TEMPLATE_FLOOR_LOCALE` and the discriminator's canonical, but hard-coded rather than imported (the module keeps itself import-free; the pin parses the result but does not compare the fallback to the constant — a drift the spec test `stack-email-template-locale-floor.test.ts` does not watch for this file). Conventions match the two siblings: the `RowForDefinition` interface with an index signature, pure, deterministic key order, the "not validation" note, the `boolean | 0 | '0' | 'false'` reading inverted from `positionDefinitionFromRow`'s truthy test and documented. It does not filter through the schema's shape as `permissionSetDefinitionFromRow` does; the position mapper does not either, and the pin holds the body to a full `safeParse`. The export sits in `packages/core/src/security/index.ts` beside the other two with its type, and core's root index re-exports `./security`, so it is on the `.` surface the changeset grades. The test's `@objectstack/spec/system` subpath is exported by spec's package.json. The file lives under `security/` because the card put the mappers there; semantically it is a template, not a security object — nit.

7. **Data safety.** No write precedes the backup acknowledgement and the boot: the command's flow is unchanged and both steps run inside `applyOrganizationOwnership` after the plan. No SQL is built from data: `templatePromotionSql` quotes through `Sql.q` and binds `true` and the three provenance words; the move quotes every column it copies (names from the driver's column listing, each refused by `SAFE_IDENTIFIER` if unsafe) and binds ids and the where's values; the command's `find` is a constant statement with six bound values. Destructive steps: the template DELETE is fate 2 after the promotion (with F2's hole); the settings DELETE is the `moved` departure the inventory names under D7 and #15207's ruling; the sharing-rule mirrors are not touched.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22937-core-email-template-row-definition.md` grades `@objectstack/core` **`minor`** and `.changeset/22937-cli-ceremony-promotions.md` grades `@objectstack/cli` **`minor`**; both carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, as does line 2 of the PR body. Under the WHICH LEVEL rule in `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`, a new exported symbol on an index (core: `emailTemplateDefinitionFromRow` and its row type, reachable from the package root) and a new accepted key on a published payload (cli: `tables[].movedOut`, `tables[].movedIn`, two new `steps[].step` values, the `template-promotion` departure id in the report file and `--json` stdout) each take at least `minor`; the commit type `feat(` agrees. `Check Changeset` is `success`, so the level axis accepted a declared clause ② with both moved packages at `minor`. Hidden removal or narrowing: none on a public surface — `ApplyOptions.templates` is a new required option, but `organization-ownership-apply.ts` is not on the CLI's `exports` (`.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`) and is imported only by the command and two tests in the package; no flag, exit code or key is removed; the one behavioural tightening (under `single`, template rows PR 2 kept are deleted after promotion) is the ceremony completing, stated in the cli changeset. Both changeset bodies match the code on every clause read, including the walled posture and the `alreadyMoved` rule. No BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 entry is owed by this PR; the `sys_email_template` table's own retirement under D13 is C8's entry, not this one.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **F1 — blocking on this head, the seat's remedy. The closing-target claim gate is red.** `scripts/check-closing-target-claim.mjs` exits 1 when no `Claim:` comment on the card this PR closes carries a `Branch:` directive naming the PR's head branch (`claimedBranches` reads `Branch:` lines only). The only claim on #22937 is 6122368393, `Branch: claude/issue-22937-organization-ownership-apply`; this PR's branch is `claude/issue-22937-ceremony-promotions`, and the dispatch 6151180611 said "The claim 6122368393 stands". The script forbids the dispatched executor from posting a second claim ("the dispatch's claim is its identity"), so the seat posts a `Claim:` on #22937 naming this branch and re-runs the job; the gate reads the card live, so no new head is needed for it. The job log itself is NOT MEASURED (the proxy refuses the log host); the cause is read from the script and the thread.
- **F2 — blocking-grade, the dev's remedy; the seat decides whether it lands in this PR.** Under `single` the template DELETE is `WHERE 1 = 1` and nothing before it checks that each row has its environment copy (①2, ①3): a nameless row is reported and then deleted, and on a resumed run every row present is deleted with no promotion re-read, including a row customized or authored between the runs. This is the B1 class (a customer row deleted without promotion) through a narrow window — the same window PR 2 closed for grants with the gate re-read, on this card, and pinned. Remedy inside the surface: before the first template DELETE under `single`, run the promotion pass again (it is idempotent: equal bodies are `alreadyPromoted`) and block if it promotes nothing new while a population row lacks a copy — or delete by id (the promoted ids plus the seeded mirrors) and block on any other row; make the nameless-row arm a blocker; add a pin that inserts a customized row between the killed run and the resume and asserts it survives.
- **Dev deviations (6153947869), answered:** the `customized NULL` population — right (①2); the two merge commits and the default message — accepted, as 6140351542 accepted the same shape. No open questions and no out-of-scope findings were reported.
- **Walled posture, escalated.** ADR-0131 section 6 Q1 as ruled (C) says the ceremony promotes customer-edited templates and, on a deployment with more than one organization, lists a name conflict for the operator to choose per row (fate 4). PR 3 promotes nothing under a wall and counts every population row as remaining forever (the dispatch's item 2 asked for exactly that count). As built, a walled deployment holding any customized or authored template cannot reach `verified_at` through this ceremony, and no PR or card in the inputs carries the walled promotion with the per-row choice. The seat names a carrier (or rules that walled deployments resolve the rows by hand, which the face names).
